alt: Poster: record FPI net equity buying Rs 99,158 crore in November to 17 Nov vs previous record Rs 70,896 crore (Nov 2020); Sensex 82,031.81 (-0.61%) on 18 Nov 2026
text:
Foreign investors have bought a record amount of Indian equities in November, even as the Sensex fell on Wednesday.

• FPIs made net equity purchases of Rs 99,158 crore in November through 17 Nov, per NSDL and exchange provisional data as reported by Business Standard and Angel One.
• The previous monthly record was Rs 70,896 crore in November 2020, per the same reports.
• This follows net FPI selling of Rs 2.95 trillion in equities between January and October 2026, per NSDL data.
• On 18 Nov the Sensex closed at 82,031.81, down 0.61%, with the Nifty Midcap 100 down 1.22% and the Nifty Smallcap 100 down 0.35%, per Business Standard and Kotak Neo closing reports.

Our view: a record month of foreign buying and a down day for the index are not contradictory, since flows are one input among several, including domestic flows, valuations and global cues. We read this as a reminder that a single day's index move says little about the direction of flows. This is an interpretation of the data, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: how much weight do you give monthly FPI flow data when judging market breadth, versus domestic flows and earnings?
